overclaims: Treating any residual error as proof that a problem is unsolved would impose a stricter standard than Marcus supplied.
checks.note: Axis, outcome and the 2020 to 2024-03-10 period match. The rationale says Marcus 'supplied' a standard, but he gave none. The 'reliably overcoming, not zero errors' standard is the evaluator's interpretation, and the contract flags that 'solved' has no threshold. Also, e1's excerpt is cut to '52.7% accuracy', which drops the 16.8% comparison for the 7.1B model, so the cited words no longer show a gain from scaling. The e2 fragment is accurate.

The excerpt is verbatim, including the 'Still true' endorsement. The proposition is faithful. Axis and outcome (not_applicable / not_adjudicable) match the reviews. The rationale correctly says one high-stakes trial does not refute a relative claim. The e1 excerpt, dates (enrollment cutoff 2022-07-28, published 2023-08-01) and context relation are correct. The interim-analysis and human-plus-AI limitation is consistent with the trial text. A small wording point: calling the statement 'the advice' is loose but not misleading.

The limitation 'The evaluation used an API model' is not supported by any evidence item. The Proof News methods page was read but not used, and e1 never says the model was tested via API. Also, there is a tension: the revised proposition narrows the claim to the particular OpenAI effort, but the 'supported' outcome rests on the contract's broader GPT-4 reading. The payload's own limitation admits this evidence would not settle that narrower claim. The e1 citation and the January 25, 2024 date are correct.
